takeaway: Steering a frozen policy's noise, as DSRL does, only ever lands on actions the policy already makes, so a skill it never learned stays out of reach; a small edit on the action, as in EXPO, can step past them.
sentence: Changing only a robot's starting guess limits it to moves it already knows, while editing the movement can let it reach farther.
reason: Both contrast a starting-guess change restricted to learned moves with an action edit that can reach beyond them.
